title: School and Exam Stress
summary: Exam worry, pressure and comparison, rest and balance, and the support a teen has around school.
clinicianNotes: Written for teens aged 12 to 17. Consider involving parents or teachers with the teen's consent. Topic areas are informed by general published work on stress, mood and wellbeing. All items are original wording and are not copied or adapted from any instrument. Bands are provisional and not clinically validated. Use the summary to guide your own questions. Draft content: needs review by a licensed psychologist, and a topic-specific reference list should be added during that review.
prompt: Thinking about the last two weeks, how true is this for you?

domains.label: Exam worry
domains.description: Worry about marks, results and letting family down.

guidance.ok: On exam worry, things look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: On exam worry, some strain is showing. Explore when it began, what triggers it, and what the person already does about it. Ask what the teen fears will happen and where that fear came from.
guidance.explore: On exam worry, the person is strongly affected. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted. Ask what the teen fears will happen and where that fear came from.

domains.label: Pressure and comparison
domains.description: Being compared and feeling only top marks count.

guidance.ok: On pressure and comparison, things look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: On pressure and comparison, some strain is showing. Explore when it began, what triggers it, and what the person already does about it. Explore whose voices set the bar and what the teen would say back.
guidance.explore: On pressure and comparison, the person is strongly affected. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted. Explore whose voices set the bar and what the teen would say back.

domains.label: Rest and balance
domains.description: Losing sleep, meals, play and energy to studies.

guidance.ok: On rest and balance, things look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: On rest and balance, some strain is showing. Explore when it began, what triggers it, and what the person already does about it. Explore small ways to protect sleep, food and some time off.
guidance.explore: On rest and balance, the person is strongly affected. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted. Explore small ways to protect sleep, food and some time off.

domains.label: Support
domains.description: Having someone at home, school and among friends to turn to.

guidance.ok: On support, there is a strength to build on. Use it when planning next steps.
guidance.watch: On support, support is partly in place. Explore what helps and what gets in the way. Explore who could be told about the pressure, and how.
guidance.explore: On support, support looks thin. Explore what is missing, who or what could help, and small first steps. Explore who could be told about the pressure, and how.

items.text: I worry a lot about my marks and results.
My mind goes blank or I feel sick before tests.
I keep thinking I will let my family down.
I feel I am always being compared with other students.
There is never enough time to do everything.
I feel I must get top marks or I am a failure.
I stay up late studying or worrying about school.
I skip meals, sports or hobbies because of studies.
I feel tired and low in the middle of the school term.
I can tell someone at home how I feel about school.
A teacher or school adult would listen if I needed help.
I have friends I can study or relax with.
